# HeliosDB-Nano

> Apache-2.0 embedded ACID database in a single binary: PostgreSQL + MySQL wire
> compatibility, HNSW vector search, copy-on-write database branching,
> time-travel (AS OF) queries, BM25 full-text search, and a built-in MCP server
> for AI agents. Use existing clients (psql, mysql, psycopg2, JDBC, ORMs) or
> drive it entirely through MCP tool calls.

## Why agents use Nano

- `profile = "agent"` config bundle: group-commit writes + time-travel ON, so
  branch sandboxes, AS OF reads, and vector search all work out of the box.
- Branches = ephemeral fork-test-discard sandboxes: give every agent run its
  own copy-on-write branch, test destructive changes, then drop the branch.
- MCP server (`--features mcp-endpoint`) is the canonical agent path: 16 tools
  over stdio / HTTP / WebSocket JSON-RPC 2.0 — no SQL string-building needed.
- Embedded (in-process Rust) or server mode; in-memory mode for throwaway runs.

## Install

```bash
cargo install heliosdb-nano --locked            # CLI binary from crates.io
cargo add heliosdb-nano                         # embedded Rust library
# Agent-relevant optional features:
cargo install heliosdb-nano --locked --features mcp-endpoint              # MCP server
cargo install heliosdb-nano --locked --features code-graph,mcp-endpoint   # + AST index
```

npx / Homebrew / Docker are NOT active install channels yet — use Cargo.
Other features: `graph-rag` (knowledge graph), `code-embed` (local embedder),
`vector-persist` (durable HNSW), `fips`, `ha-full`. See the
`heliosdb-nano-install` skill or README "Building from Source".

## Start and connect

```bash
heliosdb-nano start --data-dir ./mydata --mysql   # PG :5432, MySQL :3306, HTTP :8080
heliosdb-nano start --memory --mysql              # in-memory (ideal for agent runs)
heliosdb-nano repl --data-dir ./mydata            # interactive REPL, zero setup
psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5432 -U postgres             # any PG client works unchanged
mysql -h 127.0.0.1 -P 3306 -u root                # any MySQL client works unchanged
curl "http://localhost:8080/rest/v1/<table>?select=*"   # REST (PostgREST-style)
```

Embedded (no server):

```rust
let db = heliosdb_nano::EmbeddedDatabase::new("./mydata")?;   // or new_in_memory()
db.execute("CREATE TABLE t (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, x TEXT)")?;
let rows = db.query("SELECT * FROM t WHERE x = $1", &["a".into()])?;
```

## Agent profile

```toml
# config.toml — pass via: heliosdb-nano start --config config.toml
profile = "agent"   # group_commit WAL + time-travel ON: branch sandboxes,
                    # AS OF queries, and HNSW vector search guaranteed enabled
```

Other profiles: `safe` (fsync everything), `balanced`, `fast` (no time-travel).
A profile only fills in `[storage]` keys you do not set explicitly; add
`durable_commit = true` if commits must survive power loss (not just crashes).
See config.example.toml for every section.

## MCP — the canonical agent path

Requires a build with `--features mcp-endpoint`. 16 tools: `heliosdb_query`,
`_schema`, `_list_tables`, `_create_table`, `_insert`,
`heliosdb_branch_{create,list,merge}`, `heliosdb_search`, `_time_travel`,
plus in-process RAG tools `_bm25_index`, `_hybrid_search`,
`heliosdb_graph_{add_edge,traverse,path}` (graph-rag), `_embed_and_store`
(code-embed).

```bash
# Wire into Claude Code:
claude mcp add heliosdb -- heliosdb-nano mcp serve --data-dir ./mydata
# HTTP / WebSocket transports for other agents:
heliosdb-nano mcp serve --data-dir ./mydata --transport http --listen 127.0.0.1:9000
```

Notes: `tools/list` returns only what is compiled in; with stdio transport never
log to stdout; `heliosdb_query` returns errors as a JSON `error` field, not an
exception; drop `agent_run_*` branches when done — they persist otherwise.
Full recipes: `.claude/skills/heliosdb-nano-mcp/SKILL.md`.

## SQL dialect notes

- Dialect autodetect: PostgreSQL syntax is canonical; MySQL type aliases
  (`DATETIME`, `AUTO_INCREMENT`, `TINYINT(1)`, …) and SQLite-isms are accepted
  (`?` placeholders, `INSERT OR REPLACE/IGNORE`, `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY
  AUTOINCREMENT`, `sqlite_master`, `PRAGMA table_info` etc.).
- Parameter styles: `?`, `$1`, `:name`, `@name` all work.
- `INSERT … ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE/NOTHING`, `INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE …
  RETURNING`, CTEs, window functions, set ops, `EXPLAIN [ANALYZE]`.
- Transactions: `BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK`, nested `SAVEPOINT … RELEASE/ROLLBACK
  TO`. Bulk-load: wrap tens of thousands of INSERTs in one transaction.
- Introspection: `information_schema.*`, `pg_class`, `sqlite_master`,
  `PRAGMA table_info(t)`, REPL `\d [table]` / `\dt`.
- JSONB operators `->`, `->>`, `@>`, `?`; FTS via `to_tsvector @@ to_tsquery`
  + `ts_rank_cd` (BM25-backed).

## Vector search

Distance operators (verified against src/sql/planner.rs + src/vector/mod.rs):

| Operator | Meaning | ORDER BY ascending returns |
|----------|---------|----------------------------|
| `<->` | L2 (Euclidean) distance | nearest first |
| `<=>` | cosine distance | most similar first |
| `<#>` | negative inner product | largest dot-product first |

```sql
CREATE TABLE docs (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT, embedding VECTOR(1536));
CREATE INDEX ON docs USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);
INSERT INTO docs (title, embedding) VALUES ('Intro', '[0.1, 0.2, ...]');

SELECT title, embedding <=> '[0.15, 0.25, ...]' AS dist
FROM docs ORDER BY dist LIMIT 10;                       -- k-NN

-- Hybrid (vector + BM25) in one query:
SELECT id, 0.7 * (1.0 - (embedding <=> $1::vector))
         + 0.3 * ts_rank_cd(to_tsvector(text), plainto_tsquery($2)) AS score
FROM chunks ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 10;
```

Durable index variant (`--features vector-persist`):
`CREATE INDEX … USING hnsw (embedding) WITH (persistent = true, quantization =
'product', rerank_precision = 'i8')`. Library bulk API: `insert_vectors` /
`delete_vectors` / `delete_vector_store`. Tuning: `[vector]` config
(`hnsw_ef_construction`, `hnsw_m`, PQ knobs).

## Branch sandboxes (fork — test — discard)

Branches are copy-on-write forks of the database — the primitive for letting an
agent execute arbitrary SQL against real data with zero write-risk to `main`.
The recommended lifecycle is fork-test-discard:

```sql
CREATE DATABASE BRANCH agent_run_42 FROM main;   -- instant copy-on-write fork
USE BRANCH agent_run_42;
-- … run migrations, destructive UPDATEs, experiments; validate with SELECTs …
USE BRANCH main;
DROP DATABASE BRANCH agent_run_42;               -- discard; main never touched
```

Optionally anchor the fork in the past: `CREATE DATABASE BRANCH b FROM main AS
OF TIMESTAMP '2026-06-01 09:00:00'` (needs time-travel ON — the agent profile
guarantees it). Library API: `create_branch` / `switch_branch` / `drop_branch`
/ `list_branches`. REPL: `\branches`, `\use <branch>`, `\show branch`.

> WARNING — MERGE is currently unreliable. `MERGE DATABASE BRANCH x INTO main`
> exists, but its three-way conflict detection over-reports and can mis-detect
> conflicts (branch keys no longer carry timestamps, so the merge-base lookup
> reads the latest value instead of the historical base). If you merge, verify
> the merged rows yourself afterwards (e.g. diff row counts and spot-check
> changed rows against the source branch). A full fix is tracked (audit C11).
> Until then, prefer fork-test-discard: apply validated changes to `main`
> directly (re-run the tested SQL) instead of merging the branch.

## Time travel

```sql
SELECT * FROM products AS OF TIMESTAMP '2026-06-01 12:00:00';
SELECT * FROM products AS OF TRANSACTION 12345;
```

Any read can be anchored to a past timestamp (audit, "what changed", recover
values from before a bad UPDATE). Requires `time_travel_enabled = true`
(default; ON in the `safe`, `balanced`, and `agent` profiles, OFF in `fast`).
REPL: `\snapshots`.

## Backup / restore

```bash
heliosdb-nano dump --data-dir ./mydata --output backup.hdb     # zstd default
heliosdb-nano restore --data-dir ./newdata --input backup.hdb
heliosdb-nano start … --dump-schedule "0 */6 * * *"            # periodic dumps
```

Library: `db.dump_full(path)` / `db.restore_from_dump(path)` /
`db.restore_tables(path, [t…])`.

## Skill catalogue (19 skills, .claude/skills/)

Per-domain operating manuals for LLM agents (Claude Code picks them up
automatically after `git clone`; install globally with
`bash scripts/install-agent-skills.sh`). Name — scope — key commands:

- heliosdb-nano-overview — top-level router to the other skills.
- heliosdb-nano-install — crates.io / source install, every cargo feature
  flag, data-dir init. `cargo install heliosdb-nano --locked`,
  `heliosdb-nano init`.
- heliosdb-nano-connect — five connection modes: embedded Rust, PG wire,
  MySQL wire, REPL, Python sqlite3 drop-in; auth + TLS. `heliosdb-nano repl`,
  `psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5432`, `mysql -h 127.0.0.1 -P 3306`.
- heliosdb-nano-schema — DDL: tables, constraints, B-tree + HNSW indexes,
  views, materialized views; introspection. `\d`, `\dt`,
  `\dS`, `\dmv`, `CREATE INDEX … USING hnsw`. Also documents why triggers
  are unimplemented (`CREATE TRIGGER` registers but never fires) and why
  user-defined functions are unusable (`CREATE FUNCTION` registers, but
  every call route errors `Unknown scalar function`). Stored procedures
  DO work: `CREATE PROCEDURE p(a INT) LANGUAGE sql AS $$… $a …$$` +
  `CALL p(1)` — must be `LANGUAGE sql`, params need the `$` sigil.
- heliosdb-nano-query — DML: INSERT (OR REPLACE/IGNORE, ON CONFLICT,
  RETURNING), UPDATE/DELETE RETURNING, parameter styles, CTEs, window
  functions, EXPLAIN [ANALYZE], result cache.
- heliosdb-nano-transactions — BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK, savepoints, RAII
  `db.begin_transaction()`, deadlock detection, bulk-load pattern.
- heliosdb-nano-branches — fork-test-discard agent sandboxes: `CREATE
  DATABASE BRANCH … FROM main [AS OF …]`, `USE BRANCH`, `DROP DATABASE
  BRANCH`; merge exists but see the MERGE warning above.
- heliosdb-nano-time-travel — `SELECT … AS OF TIMESTAMP '…'`, snapshot
  listing, bad-UPDATE recovery recipes. `\snapshots`.
- heliosdb-nano-backup — `heliosdb-nano dump`/`restore`, zstd/gzip/brotli,
  append (incremental) dumps, partial table restore, `--dump-schedule`.
- heliosdb-nano-vector — HNSW DDL, `<->` / `<#>` / `<=>` operators, bulk
  vector API, hybrid BM25+vector search, `[vector]` tuning.
- heliosdb-nano-code-graph — tree-sitter AST symbol index over a repo
  (`code-graph` feature): `code_index()`, `lsp_definition` / `lsp_references`
  / `lsp_call_hierarchy` / `lsp_hover`, `_hdb_code_*` tables, git hook
  (`heliosdb-nano code-graph hook`).
- heliosdb-nano-graph-rag — `_hdb_graph_*` knowledge-graph schema +
  seed/expand/rerank retrieval (`graph-rag` feature); ingestors for docs,
  PDF, Office, audio, images, email, issues, Q&A. `graph_rag_search(q)`.
- heliosdb-nano-mcp — the MCP server itself: transports, 16-tool catalog,
  `claude mcp add heliosdb -- heliosdb-nano mcp serve --data-dir ./mydata`.
- heliosdb-nano-server — daemon mode: `start | stop | status`, TOML config,
  auth modes (trust/password/md5/scram-sha-256), TLS, HA roles
  (primary/standby/observer), sync modes, user management.
- heliosdb-nano-tenant — multi-tenant isolation: SharedSchema+RLS,
  SchemaPerTenant, DatabasePerTenant; tiered plans, per-tenant quotas,
  `current_tenant()` RLS policies.
- heliosdb-nano-deploy — Dockerfile.binary, docker-compose, Fly.io, Railway,
  Render templates (deployment/), install script, systemd unit.
- heliosdb-nano-observability — RUST_LOG tracing, slow-query log (1 s WARN
  default), `GET /health`, `\stats`, `\compression`, `\optimize`, `\indexes`.
- heliosdb-nano-migrate — drop-in migration from SQLite (Python
  `heliosdb_sqlite` SDK), PostgreSQL (any PG client), MySQL (`--mysql`,
  WordPress/PHP); dialect gotchas.
- heliosdb-nano-merge-validation — this repo's 8-phase pre-merge validation
  methodology (contributors, not end users).

Verb lookup (every CLI flag / REPL command / Rust API / MCP tool):
`.claude/skills/_index/verb-map.md`. Feature-flag map:
`.claude/skills/_index/feature-matrix.md`.
